threads.body: Resetting to `Context.root()` drops any valid ambient span and baggage active around listener dispatch. `MessagingProcessContextCustomizer` can preserve an ambient parent only when it is present in `parentContext`, so this branch reparents the process span to the message creation context whenever no receive context exists (including the suppressed-receive path). Preserve the current context when no receive context is available.

replies.body: Updated the listener to retain `Context.current()` as `parentContext` when no receive context exists. The instrumenter temporarily makes `Context.root()` current only during remote extraction, preserving ambient span and baggage while satisfying context-leak checks.

threads.body: These assertions compare only histogram point attributes. Multiple recordings with the same attributes aggregate into one point, so a duplicate duration emission would still pass even though single ownership is a core behavior under test. Also assert that every matched point has a count of one.

replies.body: Updated `verifyHistogram` to require every matched point to have a count of one before comparing attributes, so duplicate recordings cannot pass through aggregation.

Fixed in `78bd9baa6b`. The listener now selects `parentContext` once and passes it to both `shouldStart` and `start`: the ambient context for stable messaging, or the recorded receive context for legacy mode when present.

threads.body: is activating the root context necessary? I think `shouldStart` and `start` don't look at the current context

replies.body: The root scope is still needed only for the legacy propagating instrumenter because it performs remote extraction and its context-leak guard expects a root current context. I moved `shouldStart` outside that scope and skip root activation for stable and recorded-receive paths; a focused comment explains the remaining scope.
